entities.summary: Anders Sunesen was a Danish archbishop of Lund, Scania, from 21 March 1201, at the death of Absalon, to his own death in 1228. He played a crucial role in the politics of the Holy Roman Empire, serving as a mediator between the Danish king and the emperor. Sunesen was instrumental in resolving the conflict between Denmark and the Holy Roman Empire, which had been ongoing since the 12th century. He also oversaw the construction of several churches and monasteries in Scania, leaving a lasting legacy in the region. Despite his significant contributions, Sunesen's life was marked by controversy, including allegations of heresy and conflicts with other clergy. He was eventually excommunicated by the Pope, adding to his notoriety. The exact dates of his birth and death are unknown, but it is known that he died on 1 July 1228. The influence of Anders Sunesen can still be felt today, particularly in the art and architecture of the region, where his designs and ideas continue to inspire architects and artists.
